lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.23 - A Listen, point and say

details:
Listen, point, and say checks understanding of word meaning and sound.
Listen and point shows that students can match what they hear to the right image. Say practises first-step pronunciation.
Look for careful listening, correct pointing, clear sounds and confident repetition.
“We’re at Nick’s house today. Look at all his family pictures? Can you help me say who is in them?”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.23 - B. Listen and circle

details: Listen and circle continues checking sound–image connections. Students listen for specific words or details, then show understanding by clearly circling the correct picture or number.
Look for careful listening, accurate choices, clear circling and neat work in students’ books.
“Wow - Nick has a quite a big family! Who does Amy ask about - listen with me to find out!”

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.24 - C. Ask and answer

details: Ask and answer gives students the opportunity to practice using the target language to ask and respond to simple questions.
Look for use of familial  vocabulary and taking turns. Ensure students are using the picture prompts to help them,
“Let’s find out who is in this picture, too! What questions can we ask?”

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.24 - D. Draw your family. Then, ask and answer. 10m]

details:
Draw your family gives students the chance to reflect on their learning by creating their own artwork.

Ask and answer helps develop oral confidence and fluency while practising simple question and answer exchanges.
Look for a drawing that clearly reflects people in the family, and pairs asking and answering questions with correct responses.
“Now we’re going to draw our own family pictures! Don’t leave anyone out!”
